Version 3.1 is a feature expansion release built on top of the v3.0 Gold Master. The v3.0 system stabilized all crash-level issues, fixed core calculations, and established the backend PDF server. Version 3.1 expands the system's real-world usability by making financial records more flexible, reports more useful, the UI more consistent, and the module structure more logical.
All 12 changes in this version come directly from real-world usage feedback. They are mapped precisely to the existing codebase — this is not a redesign, it is a targeted expansion.

updateRecord and deleteRecord already exist and are correct

DriverDashboard.jsx has no filter state. All stats are computed by iterating every log and salary record in the collections unconditionally. The result is a single set of lifetime totals that grows forever and never reflects a specific period.
Why This Matters for Rural Users

Agriculture in Tamil Nadu runs on seasons — Kuruvai, Samba, Thaladi. A driver wants to know 'How much did I earn in the Samba 2025 season?' or 'How many hours did I work last month?' Lifetime totals answer neither question.
Add a filter toggle at the top of DriverDashboard.jsx with two modes:
KUR = June 1 to September 30 of selected year
SAM = August 1 of selected year to January 31 of selected year+1
THA = October 1 of selected year to January 31 of selected year+1
Filter logs: log.date falls within the season date range AND log.driverId === userId
Filter salary: salary.date falls within the season date range AND salary.driverId === userId
Filter logs: new Date(log.date).getMonth()+1 === selectedMonth && getFullYear() === selectedYear
Filter salary: same logic on salary.date
On first load: Mode B (By Month), current month and year. Driver sees their current month's stats immediately without any interaction.
Fix session time defaults — empty inputs, correct trigger

This means every new log entry already has 1 hour pre-calculated. A driver who does not notice the pre-filled times and saves immediately will create an incorrect log entry. After a save, the reset also restores the same pre-filled defaults. There is no indication to the driver that they must change these values.
The Calculation Trigger (How It Works Now)

The handleSessionChange function checks: if (start && end) → calculate getDuration(). This logic is correct — it fires whenever either field changes as long as the other is non-empty. The only problem is the pre-filled values bypass this trigger visually.

With empty defaults, the duration shows 0.00 until the driver fills in both times. Once start and end are both non-empty, getDuration() fires and the result appears immediately without needing to touch any field a second time.

Two sub-modules + salary logic fully decoupled from driver logs

Drivers.jsx becomes a tabbed module with two sub-modules. The standalone SalaryDriver.jsx route is removed. The App.jsx /salary-driver route is removed. The driver nav now shows 'My Salary' which renders Drivers.jsx with the salary tab pre-selected and restricted to the logged-in driver's userId.

The current SalaryDriver.jsx scans for driver logs without a linkedSalaryId. If availableLogs.length === 0, it immediately blocks with an alert and prevents saving. This creates a hard dependency: the salary module cannot record ANY payment unless there are unpaid driver logs available. Real scenarios this breaks:
Admin wants to give a Diwali bonus: zero logs unpaid → blocked
Admin wants to record a ₹500 advance before any work starts → blocked
Admin wants to note extra pay for a driver who helped with non-machine work → blocked
Driver worked but log entry was not created yet → blocked
New Salary Logic — Fully Independent Entries
Each salary entry is a standalone financial record. There is no dependency on driver logs. Admin can create a salary entry for any combination of base, bonus, extra, and advance at any time.
// New salary entry schema (saved to rl_driver_salary):
baseSalary: 1200, // 0 if not this entry type
// netPay is computed on render, NOT stored:
payments: [] // partial payment tracking (same pattern as Harvester)

At least one of baseSalary, bonus, extraAmount, or advance must be > 0. If all four are 0 and Save is tapped, show inline Tamil error: 'குறைந்தது ஒரு தொகை தேவை (At least one amount is required)'. All four can be filled simultaneously in one entry — this is the normal combined salary entry. Any single field can be filled alone — this allows bonus-only, advance-only, or extra-only entries.

Net Pay is shown live as the user types: (baseSalary + bonus + extraAmount) - advance. If the result is negative (advance exceeds total earnings), show: 'முன்பணம் சம்பளத்தை விட அதிகமாக உள்ளது' with a red background. Negative net pay is allowed to save — it represents a carry-forward advance situation.

After a salary record is saved, admin can record partial payments against it using the PaymentHistory component (already built and working). This is the same pattern used in Harvester jobs and Rental entries. sumPayments(salary.payments) gives total paid. balance = netPay - sumPayments. Driver can view balance but cannot add payments.

C12 — Multi-Worker Entry (Same Work, Same Day)

This change comes from the real-world pattern where large agricultural tasks (fertilizing, transplanting seedlings — naatru nattal, kalai yeduthal, andai vettuthal) are done by multiple workers simultaneously. Recording them one by one is time-consuming and error-prone.
Workers.jsx saves one entry per form submission with a workerName string. To record 5 workers doing the same work, admin must fill the form 5 separate times. This is the root pain point.

7. Admin Edit and Delete Driver Log Entries (C11)
Admin can edit or delete any driver log entry with cascade guard

Drivers enter logs in the field, often on small mobile screens. Mistakes happen — wrong farmer selected, wrong machine type, incorrect time. Currently there is no way to fix a log after it is saved. The admin has no edit or delete capability on driver log entries. This creates permanent incorrect data in the system.

In DriverEntry.jsx, the 'Today's Logs' section at the bottom of the page already shows saved logs. The admin view of this page should show ALL logs (not just today's), with edit and delete buttons per entry. Drivers see their own logs as before (today's only, no edit/delete).
